cases.abstract: VoxPoser turns language-specified manipulation subtasks into spatial objectives by assigning voxel values that attract an end-effector, object, or object part toward goals and repel it from obstacles. Generated programs query visual perception to ground these maps, letting motion planners optimize desired motion and constraints jointly instead of requiring language models to specify action parameters directly. Observation-based replanning enables zero-shot execution without additional training. Across five real-world tasks, success is 88% in static scenes and 70% under disturbances, versus 24% and 0% for an LLM using simple primitives, supporting spatial composition over sequential primitive specification. Across 13 simulated tasks, category averages favor VoxPoser on seen and unseen instructions and attributes, although individual tasks favor baselines. For three simulated contact-rich tasks, synthesized trajectories also restrict exploration to locally perturbed waypoints: online dynamics learning raises success from 3.3-18.3% to 80.0-91.7% with mean interaction times below three minutes, while exploration without priors exceeds 12 hours. This contrast supports task-directed adaptation when zero-shot plans are insufficient; perception errors, restricted environment dynamics, and end-effector-only planning delimit the demonstrated capabilities.
cases.notes: Retained trajectory synthesis and simulator-only dynamics learning as distinct contributions. The real-world primitive comparison tests whether spatial objectives support execution; the exploration-prior comparison tests adaptation when initial plans fail. Category-level transfer gains remain bounded by per-task reversals. No isolated causal claim is inferred from the component comparisons. Perception, dynamics scope, and end-effector planning remain limiting conditions.

cases.abstract: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) addresses training minima with similar losses but different test performance by optimizing the worst training loss within a parameter neighborhood. A conditional PAC-Bayesian bound motivates the objective, assuming Gaussian weight perturbations do not lower population loss and Euclidean weight norm is at least one, without certifying approximate minibatch updates. The practical optimizer uses one gradient to choose a loss-increasing perturbation and another at perturbed weights to update the original parameters. Across tested CIFAR configurations, SAM improves generalization even when non-SAM baselines can train for twice as many epochs, supporting a benefit beyond longer point-loss optimization. Lower measured Hessian curvature in the tested model also supports the intended neighborhood geometry. Gains extend to ImageNet ResNets and EfficientNet finetuning after ImageNet or ImageNet-plus-JFT pretraining. Under random label noise, unbootstrapped SAM improves clean-test accuracy over SGD but trails reported MentorMix results; one augmented SVHN configuration regresses. A complementary analysis evaluates sharpness through separate loss maximizations on subsets, defining m-sharpness. Smaller subsets improve generalization in the studied training setting and predict generalization gaps better than full-training-set sharpness.
cases.notes: Prioritized whether neighborhood-loss optimization improves generalization beyond extra standard training, with Hessian evidence testing the intended geometry. Retained the conditional population-loss bound separately from approximate updates and the m-sharpness finding separately from optimizer performance. EfficientNet gains retain pretraining provenance; unbootstrapped noise results retain the literature comparator and the SVHN exception. Subset comparisons show that theorem-motivated full-data sharpness is not the strongest predictor in these evaluations.
